6.102.d:
इतिश्रीपाद्मेमहापुराणेपंचपंचाशत्सहस्रसंहितायामुत्तरखंडेकार्त्तिकमाहात्म्ये
श्रीकृष्णसत्यभामासंवादेदैत्यकपटवर्णनोनामद्व्यधिकशततमोऽध्यायः
त्र्यधिकशततमोऽध्यायःनारदौवाचविष्णुर्जालंधरंगत्वातद्दैत्यपुटभेदनम्
पातिव्रत्यस्यभंगायवृंदायाश्चाकरोन्मतिम्
अथवृंदारकादेवीस्वप्नमध्येददर्शह
भर्त्तारंमहिषारूढं तैलाभ्यक्तंदिगंबरम्
कृष्णप्रसूनभूषाढ्यंक्रव्यादगणसेवितम्
दक्षिणाशांगतंमुंडंतमसाव्यावृतंतदा
स्वपुरंसागरेमग्नंसहसैवात्मनासह
ततःप्रबुद्धासाबालास्वस्वप्नंप्रविचिन्वती
ददर्शोदितमादित्यंसच्छिद्रंनिश्चलंमुहुः
तदनिष्टमितिज्ञात्वारुदतीभयविह्वला
कुत्रचिन्नालभच्छर्मगोपुराट्टालभूमिषु
ततःसखीद्वययुतानगरोद्यानमागमत्
तत्रापिसागताबालानालभत्कुत्रचित्सुखम्
वनाद्वनांतरंयातानैववेदात्मनस्तदा
6.102.m: Thus ends the one hundred and first chapter, entitled "The Defeat of the Daitya Army," in the dialogue between glorious Kṛṣṇa and Satyabhāmā, in the Kārttikamāhātmya of the Uttarakhaṇḍa in the glorious Padma Mahāpurāṇa, in the collection of fifty-five thousand [verses].

6.102.d:
ततोभ्रमंतेसाबालाददर्शातिविभीषणौ
राक्षसौसिंहवदनौदंष्ट्रानयनभीषणौ
तौदृष्ट्वाविह्वलातीवपलायनपरातदा
ददर्शतापसंशांतंसशिष्यंमौनमास्थितम्
ततस्तत्कंठआसज्यनिजांबाहुलतांभयात्
मुनेमांरक्षशरणमागतामित्यभाषत
मुनिस्तांविह्वलांदृष्ट्वाराक्षसानुगतांतदा
हुंकारेणैवतौघोरौचकारविमुखौरुषा
यद्धुंकारभयत्रस्तौदृष्ट्वातौगगनंगतौ
प्रणम्यदंडवद्भूमौवृंदावचनमब्रवीत्
वृंदोवाच
रक्षिताहंत्वयाघोराद्भयात्तस्मात्कृपानिधे
किंचिद्विज्ञप्तुमिच्छामिकृपयातन्निशामय
जलंधरोहिमेभर्त्तारुद्रंयोद्धुंगतःप्रभो
सतत्रास्तिकथंयुद्धेतन्मेकथयसुव्रत
नारदौवाचमुनिस्तद्वाक्यमाकर्ण्यकृपयोर्ध्वमवैक्षत
तावत्कपीशावायातौतंप्रणम्याग्रतःस्थितौ
ततस्तद्भ्रूलतासंज्ञानियुक्तौगगनंगतौ
गत्वाक्षणार्द्धादागत्यवानरावग्रतःस्थितौ

6.102.d:
शिरःकबंधहस्तौतौदृष्ट्वाब्धितनयस्यसा
पपातमूर्छिताभूमौभर्तृव्यसनदुःखिता
कमंडलुजलैःसिक्तामुनिनाश्वासितातदा
स्वभर्तृभालेसाभालंकृत्वाखिन्नारुरोदह
वृंदोवाचयःपुरासुखसंवादैर्विनोदयसिमांविभो
सकथंनवदस्यद्यवल्लभांमामनागसम्
येनदेवाःसगंधर्वानिर्जिताहरिणासह
सकथंतापसेनत्वं त्रैलोक्यविजयीहतः
नारदौवाचरुदित्वेतितदावृंदातंमुनिंवाक्यमब्रवीत्
वृंदोवाच
कृपानिधेमुनिश्रेष्ठजीवनंमेऽस्यसुप्रियम्
त्वमेवास्यपुनःशक्तोजीवनायमतोमम
अथतद्वाक्यमाकर्ण्यप्रहस्यमुनिरब्रवीत्
मुनिरुवाच
नायंजीवयितुंशक्योरुद्रेणनिहतोयुधि
तथापित्वत्कृपाविष्टएवंसंजीवयाम्यहम्
नारदौवाच
इत्युक्त्वांतर्दधेयावत्तावत्सागरनंदनः
वृंदामालिग्यतद्वक्त्रंचुचुंबेप्रीतमानसः
अथवृंदापिभर्त्तारंदृष्ट्वाहर्षितमानसा
रेमेतद्वनमध्यस्थातद्युक्ताबहुवासरम्
6.102.m: Nārada said: / Having spoken thus, he struck the bull-bannered lord with seventy arrows; / before they reached him, he severed them with sharp arrows, as if smiling.

निर्भर्त्स्यक्रोधसंयुक्तावृंदावचनमब्रवीत्

धिक्तवेदंहरेशीलंपरदाराभिगामिनः
ज्ञातोऽसित्वंमयासम्यङ्मायाप्रत्यक्षतापसः
यौत्वयामाययाद्वास्थौस्वकीयौदर्शितौमम
तावेवराक्षसौभूत्वाभार्यांतवहरिष्यथ
त्वंचापिभार्यादुःखार्तोवनेकपिसहायवान्
भ्रमसर्वेश्वरेणायंयस्तेशिष्यत्वमागतः
इत्युक्त्वासातदावृंदाप्राविशद्धव्यवाहनम्
विष्णुनावार्यमाणापितस्मिन्नासक्तमानसा
ततोहरिस्तामनुसंस्मरन्मुहुर्वृंदाचिताभस्मरजोवगुंठितः
तत्रैवतस्थौमुनिसिद्धसंघैः प्रबोध्यमानोपिययौनशांतिंम्

6.102.d:
इतिश्रीपाद्मेमहापुराणेपंचपंचाशत्सहस्रसंहितायामुत्तरखंडेकार्तिकमाहात्म्ये
श्रीकृष्णसत्यभामासंवादेवृंदाचिताग्निप्रवेशोनामत्र्यधिकशततमोऽध्यायः
चतुरधिकशततमोऽध्यायःनारदौवाचततोजलंधरोदृष्ट्वारुद्रमद्भुतविक्रमम्
चकारमाययागौरींत्र्यबकंमोहयंस्तदा
रथोपरिगतांदृष्ट्वारुदंतींचतदाशिवः
शुंभनिशुंभदैत्यैश्चवध्यमानांददर्शसः
गौरींतथाविधांदृष्ट्वाशिवोऽप्युद्विग्नमानसः
अवाङ्मुखःस्थितस्तूष्णींविस्मृत्यस्वपराक्रमम्
ततोजलंधरोवेगात्त्रिभिर्विव्याधसायकैः
आपुंखमग्नैस्तंरुद्रंशिरस्युरसिचोदरे
ततोजज्ञेसतांमायांविष्णुनासंप्रबोधितः
रौद्ररूपधरोजातोज्वालामालातिभीषणः
तस्यातीवमहारौद्रंरूपंदृष्ट्वामहासुराः
नशेकुःप्रमुखेस्थातुंभेजिरेचदिशोदश
ततःशापंददौदेवस्तयोःशुंभनिशुंभयोः
ममयुद्धादपक्रांतौगौर्यावध्यौभविष्यथः
6.102.m:
Thus ends the one hundred and second chapter, entitled "Description of the Daitya's Deception," in the dialogue between glorious Kṛṣṇa and Satyabhāmā, in the Kārttikamāhātmya of the Uttarakhaṇḍa in the glorious Padma Mahāpurāṇa, in the collection of fifty-five thousand [verses].

Chapter one hundred and three. / Nārada said: / Viṣṇu, having gone to Jalandhara, the city of that Daitya, / set his mind upon breaking the fidelity of Vṛndā.

बांणांधकारसंच्छन्नंयथाभूमितलंमहत्
यावद्रुद्रःप्रचिच्छेदतस्यबाणांस्त्वरान्वितः
तावत्सपरिघेणाशुजघानवृषभंबली
वृषस्तेनप्रहारेणपरावृत्तोरणांगणात्
रुद्रेणाकृष्यमाणोऽपिनतस्थौरणभूमिषु
ततःपरमसंक्रुद्धोरुद्रोरौद्रवपुर्द्धरः
चक्रंसुदर्शनंवेगाच्चिक्षेपादित्यवर्चसम्
प्रदहद्रोदसीवेगात्तदासाद्यजलंधरम्
जहारतच्छिरःकायान्महदायतलोचनम्
रथात्कायःपपातोर्व्यांनादयन्वसुधातलम्
तेजश्चनिर्गतंदेहात्तद्रुद्रेलयमागमत्
दृष्ट्वादेहोद्भवंतेजस्तद्गौरीशेलयंगतम्
अथचेंद्रादयोदेवाहर्षादुत्फुल्ललोचनाः
प्रणम्यशिरसारुद्रंशशंसुर्विष्णुचेष्टितम्
देवाऊचुः
महादेवत्वयादेवारक्षिताःशत्रुजाद्भयात्

6.102.m:
Thus ends the one hundred and third chapter, entitled "Vṛndā's Entry into the Funeral Fire," in the dialogue between glorious Kṛṣṇa and Satyabhāmā, in the Kārttikamāhātmya of the Uttarakhaṇḍa in the glorious Padma Mahāpurāṇa, in the collection of fifty-five thousand [verses].

Chapter one hundred and four. / Nārada said: / Then Jalandhara, seeing Rudra of wonderful valor, / created Gaurī by illusion, bewildering the three-eyed god.

6.103.m:
Thus ends the one hundred and fourth chapter, entitled "The Slaying of Jālaṃdhara," in the dialogue between glorious Kṛṣṇa and Satyabhāmā, in the Kārttikamāhātmya of the Uttarakhaṇḍa in the glorious Padma Mahāpurāṇa, in the collection of fifty-five thousand [verses].

Even the four-faced god [Brahmā] would not be able to utter / the glorification of the emblic myrobalan and the tulasī, just as of the bow-wielding god [Viṣṇu].

6.106.m: Pṛthu said: / O brāhmaṇa, this glorification was related by you accompanied by legendary history; / the great, exceedingly wondrous [tale] of the tulasī was properly heard.
The great fruit of a man who observes the Kārtika vow has been proclaimed; / tell that glorification again: by whom was this performed, and how?
Nārada said: / Formerly, in the region of the Sahya mountain, in the town of Karavīrapura, / there was a certain brāhmaṇa named Dharmadatta, who knew dharma and was very famous.
He constantly performed the vows of Viṣṇu, was always devoted to the worship of Viṣṇu, / dedicated to muttering the twelve-syllable mantra, and hospitable to guests.
Once, during the month of Kārtika, in order to keep a vigil for Hari, / when the fourth quarter of the night remained, he went to the temple of Hari.
As he was walking, carrying the utensils for the worship of Hari, / he saw an approaching rākṣasī making a terrifying sound.
She had curved fangs, a sunken tongue, red eyes, / was naked, with dried-up flesh, hanging lips, and a rattling voice.
Seeing her, terrified with fear, his limbs trembling, / he swiftly struck [her] out of fear with the worship utensils and with water.
Remembering the name of Hari, with water mixed with tulasī / she was struck; because of that, all her sin came to an end.
Then, remembering her previous birth born of the ripening of actions, / she bowed to him like a staff and recounted her entire state:
Kalahā said: / Through the ripening of past actions, I have reached this state; / how then, O brāhmaṇa, may I attain an auspicious, exalted destination?
Nārada said: / Seeing her bowed before him, recounting that karma of hers, / the brāhmaṇa, greatly astonished, then spoke these words:
Dharmadatta said: / Through the ripening of what action did you reach such a state? / From where are you, who are you, and of what conduct? Tell all that to me.
Kalahā said: / In the city of Saurāṣṭra, O brāhmaṇa, there was a twice-born named Bhikṣu; / formerly, I was his housewife, named Kalahā, exceedingly cruel.
Never was any good done by me, even in word, for my husband; / sweet food was never offered to him, violating my husband's words.
Ever agitated with fear because of [me,] who was fond of strife, the twice-born, / my husband, then made up his mind to marry another woman.
Thereupon, taking poison, my life was cast away by me, O twice-born; / then, binding me as I was being seized, the followers of Yama carried me off.
Seeing me then, Yama questioned Citragupta. / Yama said: / 'Look, Citragupta, what deed has been done by this woman?
Let her attain the fruit of her actions, whether auspicious or inauspicious.' / Then Citragupta, rebuking [me], spoke these words:
Citragupta said: / 'No good deed whatsoever was done by this woman; / sweet food was eaten by her, but was not offered to her husband.
Therefore, let her dwell in the womb of a she-bat, eating her own excrement; / for she hated her husband and constantly caused quarrels.
Then let this woman dwell in the womb of an excrement-eating sow, O Hari; / because she always ate directly from the cooking pot, constantly.
Because of that fault, [let her become] a female cat who devours the offspring born of her own kind; / and because she committed suicide out of malice toward her husband,
therefore let this most censured woman dwell among pretas and piśācas; / and then, in this manner, she must be conducted with the guards to a desert region.
There, having the form called a preta-body, let her remain for a long time; / in this way, let this woman who worked evil experience the three wombs.'
Kalahā said: / Indeed, for five hundred years I remained in the body of a preta, / constantly tormented by hunger and thirst, afflicted by my own deeds.
Then, constantly tormented by hunger, [possessing] the body of a merchant, / I came to the southern region, to the confluence of the Kṛṣṇā and Veṇyā.
As soon as I reached its bank, from his body / I was forcibly dragged far away by the attendants of Śiva and Viṣṇu.
Then, emaciated with hunger, wandering about, you were seen by me, O twice-born; / my sin has vanished through contact with the tulasī-water thrown [by you].
Therefore, have compassion, O best of twice-born: how may I attain liberation / from the three wombs that cause great dread, and from this preta body?

Hearing Kalahā's words thus, the twice-born, filled with wonder and grief born of the ripening of that karma, / his mind stirred by compassion at seeing her distress, reflected for a long time and spoke these words out of sorrow:

6.107.m: Dharmadatta said: / Sins disappear through sacred bathing sites, gifts, vows, and the like; / but for you who are in a preta body, there is no eligibility for them.
And from seeing this distress of yours, my mind is pained; / it will not find peace without rescuing you who are suffering.
And your sin is exceedingly terrible, resulting in the ripening of three wombs, / and the most reprehensible condition of a preta cannot be destroyed by other merits.
Therefore, through half the share of the merit of the Kārtika vow / that has been performed by me since birth, attain an auspicious destination.
Sacrifices, gifts, sacred bathing sites, and even vows certainly / do not in any way equal the merit of the Kārtika vow, for that is certain.
Nārada said: / Having spoken thus, as soon as that Dharmadatta sprinkled her / with water mixed with tulasī, reciting the twelve-syllable mantra,
she was instantly freed from the condition of a preta, resembling a blazing flame of fire, / and took on a divine form, illuminating the directions with her loveliness.
Then, prostrating like a staff on the earth, she bowed to that twice-born, / and then spoke these words, her voice faltering with joy:
Kalahā said: / By your grace, O best of twice-born, I am released from hell; / for me, sinking in the ocean of sin, you have truly become a boat.
Nārada said: / As she was speaking thus to the twice-born, she saw coming from the sky / a radiant aerial chariot, accompanied by attendants bearing the form of Viṣṇu.
Then she was helped into that foremost aerial chariot, served by a host of apsarases, / by the two doorkeepers, Puṇyaśīla and Suśīla.
Seeing that aerial chariot then, Dharmadatta was filled with wonder; / seeing those two endowed with meritorious forms, he fell to the ground like a staff.
Puṇyaśīla and Suśīla raised up that bowed twice-born, / congratulated him, and, endowed with dharma, spoke these words:
The two attendants said: / 'Well done, well done, O best of the twice-born! You who are ever devoted to Viṣṇu, / compassionate to the wretched, knower of dharma, dedicated to the vows of Viṣṇu!
By giving half of this auspicious vow of Kārttika that you have performed / since birth, that which had been accumulated by her in the past—
the sin born of hundreds of other births—has vanished; / and through keeping vigil for Hari and other deeds, this aerial chariot has arrived.
The abode of Vaikuṇṭha, proximity to Viṣṇu, and possessing his form [are attained]. / Blessed are they, their purpose achieved, and fruitful is their birth,
by whom Viṣṇu has been worshipped with devotion, as by you, O Dharmadatta! / What does Viṣṇu not grant to embodied beings when properly worshipped?
He by whom the son of Uttānapāda was long ago established in the pole-star position; / simply by remembering whose name embodied beings reach the good path.
The lord of elephants, seized by a crocodile, was freed long ago by remembering his name, / and, having reached his presence, became the one named Jaya.
Therefore Viṣṇu, worshipped by you, will grant his proximity / to you along with your two wives for many thousands of years.
Then, when your merit is exhausted and you go down to the earthly realm, / you will become a famous king born in the Solar dynasty.
Named Daśaratha there, [accompanied] again with two wives, / and with a third one who was the sharer in half your merit.
There too Viṣṇu will attain proximity to you on the surface of the earth, / making himself your son, performing the work of the immortals.
From this lifelong vow of yours that causes Viṣṇu's satisfaction, / sacrifices, gifts, and holy bathing-places are not superior.
Blessed are you, O devout Brahmin! You have performed this vow bringing satisfaction to the Guru of the universe, / from the half share of whose fruit she is being led by us to the realm of Murāri.'

6.108.m: Nārada said: / Having thus heard their word, Dharmadatta, full of wonder, / bowed like a staff on the earth and spoke this word:
Dharmadatta said: / 'All people worship Viṣṇu, the destroyer of the distress of devotees, / with sacrifices, gifts, vows, holy bathing-places, and austerities according to rule.
What among these brings pleasure to Viṣṇu and brings about proximity to Viṣṇu, / by doing which all of them are indeed observed?'
The two attendants said: / 'Well asked by you, O Brahmin! Listen with a one-pointed mind / to the ancient story accompanied by legendary history being narrated, O Brahmin!
Formerly in Kāñcīpurī there was an emperor king of the Colas, / by whose name those regions indeed became known as Cola.
While he ruled the circle of the earth, no man was poor or distressed, / nor of sinful mind, nor diseased.
For him who performed many sacrifices, both banks of the Tāmraparṇī / were adorned with golden sacrificial posts, resembling the Caitraratha garden.
Once upon a time, that king went to Anantaśayana, O twice-born, / where that Lord of the worlds rests in yogic sleep.
Worshipping the god, the beloved of Śrī, according to rule with divine jewels and pearls / and beautiful golden flowers,
and bowing like a staff, as long as he sat there, / he saw a Brahmin coming into the presence of the god,
coming to worship the god, with tulasī and water in his hand, / a resident of his own city, a twice-born named Viṣṇudāsa.
Approaching there, that sage among Brahmins worshipped the God of gods; / having bathed him with the Viṣṇusūkta, [he worshipped] with tulasī blossoms and leaves.
Seeing his jewel-worship thus covered over by that [Brahmin's] tulasī-worship, / the king became angry and spoke these words:
The king said: / Here, a splendid worship with rubies and gold was performed by me; / O Viṣṇudāsa, how has it been covered over with tulasī leaves?
You do not know devotion to Viṣṇu; you are considered wretched by me, / who covers this exceedingly splendid worship, alas!'
Having heard those words of his, that best of the twice-born was filled with wrath; / transgressing respect for the king, he then spoke these words:
Viṣṇudāsa said: / 'O king, you do not know liberation; you are proud of royal fortune! / What vow of Viṣṇu has been performed by you in the past? Speak that!'
The two attendants said: / 'Having heard the Brahmin's words, that best of kings laughed, / and out of pride then spoke words to Viṣṇudāsa, O twice-born:
"If you speak thus, O Brahmin, being overly proud of your devotion to Viṣṇu: / how great is the devotion to Viṣṇu of one who is poor and penniless?
Neither sacrifice, gifts, and the like, which cause satisfaction to Viṣṇu, have been done, / nor has a temple of the god ever been built by you anywhere, O Brahmin!
Even being of such a sort, this pride of yours exists on account of devotion! / Let all these best of the twice-born listen to my word today:
Direct perception of Viṣṇu will come to me. This argument / will be resolved, and then all of you will know the devotion of the two of us."
The two attendants said: / Having said this, that king, going to his own royal residence, O twice-born, / began a Vaiṣṇava sacrificial session, having made Mudgala his priest.
It was attended by crowds of sages and had large sacrificial gifts, / like that prosperous one performed by Brahmā in the Gaya field long ago.
Viṣṇudāsa also, observant of vows, stayed right there in the temple of the god, / having undertaken these five rules which ever cause satisfaction to Viṣṇu:
The proper vow of Māgha and Kārttika, the tending of the tulasī grove, / the Ekādaśī vow, and recitation with the twelve-syllable mantra;
likewise, the daily worship of Viṣṇu with the sixteen offerings / accompanied by auspicious songs, dances, and so forth—these vows he performed.
Constantly remembering Viṣṇu while walking, eating, and even sleeping, / he, having equal vision, saw Viṣṇu residing in all beings.
In Māgha and Kārttika he also constantly observed / special rules and the rite of completion to satisfy Viṣṇu.
Thus, as those two—the lord of the Colas and Viṣṇudāsa—worshipped the husband of Śrī, / established in vows, with the actions of their sense-organs devoted to him, much time passed.

6.109.m: Thus ends the one hundred and eighth chapter, in the Episode of Kalahā, in the dialogue between glorious Kṛṣṇa and Satyabhāmā, in the Kārttikamāhātmya of the Uttarakhaṇḍa in the glorious Padma Mahāpurāṇa, in the collection of fifty-five thousand [verses].

6.110.m: Then, as he rose, Viṣṇudāsa beheld that very person / as Lord Nārāyaṇa in visible form, bearing the conch, discus, and mace,
Seeing Viṣṇudāsa going to the abode of Vaikuṇṭha, / he hastily summoned his guru Mudgala and spoke these words:

Thus ends the one hundred and ninth chapter, entitled "The Episode of Kalahā," in the dialogue between glorious Kṛṣṇa and Satyabhāmā, in the Kārttikamāhātmya of the collection of fifty-five thousand [verses] in the glorious Padma Mahāpurāṇa.

Thus ends the one hundred and tenth chapter, entitled "Description of the Previous Merit of the Gaṇas," in the Episode of Kalahā, in the dialogue between glorious Kṛṣṇa and Satyabhāmā, in the Kārttikamāhātmya of the Uttarakhaṇḍa in the glorious Padma Mahāpurāṇa, in the collection of fifty-five thousand [verses].

6.111.m:
Pṛthu said:
Since you related that previously, on the bank of the Kṛṣṇā-Veṇyā,
Kalahā was produced from a merchant's body by the attendants of Śiva and Viṣṇu,

is this the power of those two rivers, or of that holy site?
Tell me that, knower of dharma; great is my wonder in this matter.

Nevertheless, I will recount their origin; hear that:
formerly, during the Cākṣuṣa Manvantara, the god, the grandfather [Brahmā],

undertook to perform a sacrifice on a lovely peak of the Sahya mountain;
having gathered the sacrificial requisites, surrounded by the hosts of all the gods,

accompanied by Hari and Hara, he went to the peak of that mountain.
The hosts of sages, Bhṛgu and others, at the moment sacred to Brahmā,

convened an assembly there for the purpose of the initiation rite.
Then, through the brāhmaṇas, Viṣṇu summoned [Brahmā's] eldest wife, Svarā.

She came very slowly, whereupon Bhṛgu said to Viṣṇu:
Bhṛgu said:
O Viṣṇu, Svarā was summoned by you, but she does not come quickly.

And the auspicious moment is passing; how is the initiation rite to be performed?
Viṣṇu said:
If Svarā does not come quickly, let Gāyatrī be placed here.

Is she not also his wife in meritorious rites?
Nārada said:
Rudra, too, concurred with Viṣṇu's word in just this way.

Hearing that speech, Bhṛgu then seated Gāyatrī
on the right side of Brahmā and performed the initiation rite.

Just as they were duly performing the initiation rite for the Creator,
Svarā arrived there at the place of sacrifice, O king.

Then, seeing Gāyatrī initiated together with Brahmā,
Svarā, consumed with jealousy toward a co-wife, spoke words in anger.

Svarā said:
Where those unworthy of worship are worshipped, and those worthy of worship are transgressed,
three things shall arise there: famine, death, and fear.

This younger woman has been placed by you upon my seat;
therefore, turning into inert water, you shall all take various forms.

And she who has sat down upon my seat on the right side,
let her body, therefore, flowing as a river, be ever invisible to the people.

'Just as Brahmā is your husband, so indeed is he mine as well;
because you cursed me in vain, you too become a river!'

Nārada said:
Then all the gods, led by Śiva and Viṣṇu, cried out in distress:
'Then these three worlds will surely go to destruction!'

then these three worlds will surely go to destruction.
A lack of judgment was shown; therefore, let this curse be revoked!

Svarā said:
Because the lord of the hosts was not worshipped at the beginning of the sacrifice, O foremost of gods,
this obstacle, born of my anger, has indeed arisen.

Nor indeed can this word of mine become untrue;
therefore, turning into inert water through your portions, become rivers.

We two co-wives also, O gods, by our own portions,
shall become rivers here, flowing westward.

Nārada said:
Having heard her words, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśvara
then turned into inert matter and became rivers through their own portions, O king.

There Viṣṇu became the Kṛṣṇā, the god Maheśvara became the Veṇyā,
and Brahmā then became separately the Kakudminī Gaṅgā.

The gods also, having turned their portions into inert water in an instant,
became distinct fine rivers from the peaks of the Sahya mountain.

The best of rivers flowing eastward arose from the portions of the gods,
while Gāyatrī and Svarā then flowed westward.

Through spiritual concentration, the two became rivers renowned as Sāvitrī;
both Hari and Hara were established there at the sacrifice by Brahmā.

Whoever hears of the sins-destroying, supreme origin of the Kṛṣṇā, and whoever recites it with devotion,
for him every action becomes meritorious, yielding the fruit that arises from seeing and bathing in it.

6.112.m:
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said:
Having heard that speech, Pṛthu, his mind filled with wonder,
worshipped Nārada with devotion and then sent him away, O beloved.

Therefore, this triad of vows is exceedingly dear to me:
those of Māgha and Kārtika, and likewise the vow of Ekādaśī.

Among plants, tulasī is dear to me; among months, Kārtika;
among lunar days, Ekādaśī; and among sacred sites, Dvārakā.

Whoever, with senses conquered, attends upon these,
attains dearness to me, not so much by sacrifices and the like.

No fear of sins should be entertained, even through lack of vows,
by those who attend upon these, O beloved, through my grace.

Satyabhāmā said:
This is astonishing, O Lord, what you have related to me,
that by merit transferred by another, Kalahā reached liberation.

Such is the power of this month of Kārttika that pleases you,
in that sins such as betraying one's husband were removed by bathing and giving gifts.

And one receives the merit that was bestowed, performed by another, O all-pervading Lord.
By what manner does a human also receive that which was not bestowed?

The venerable Kṛṣṇa said:
How even merit and demerit that have not been bestowed
are obtained by men through action—listen to that as it truly is.

In the Kṛta age and the others, the country, village, and family would share [in deeds];
but in the Kali age, only the doer experiences the fruit of merit and demerit.

Even when there is no association, this rule is declared [for each age].
Learn how merit and demerit pass [from one to another] through association:

From having sexual intercourse together, from traveling [in one vehicle], or eating from the same vessel,
a mortal receives half the fruit of merit and demerit, as it is.

From teaching, from officiating at sacrifice, or from dining in the same row,
a person constantly receives a fourth share of merits and demerits.

From sitting on the same seat, traveling together, and contact of bodies through breath,
one becomes a recipient of a sixth share of merit and demerit, indeed.

From touching, from conversing, or even from praising another,
a mortal constantly receives a tenth share of merits and demerits.

Through looking, listening, and mental contemplation as well,
a man receives a hundredth share of another's merits and demerits.

Whoever reviles another, slanders, or scorns [him],
incurs the sin committed by him and gives away his own merit.

Whatever person serves one who performs meritorious deeds—
any person other than the wife, servant, and disciples—

the server indeed incurs a sixth part of that person's sin.
Whoever touches or speaks to one while he is performing his bath, twilight prayers, and the like,

gives a sixth share of his meritorious deed to him; this is quite certain.
Whoever solicits wealth from another with the purpose of performing dharma,

the giver of that wealth obtains the fruit born of that meritorious act.
Whoever performs a meritorious deed after seizing another's wealth,

the doer of the deed incurs the sin, while the owner of the wealth gets the fruit resulting from it.
A man who dies without discharging his debt to another—

the creditor takes his merit in proportion to his wealth.
One who advises, one who consents, and one who provides the means,

as well as the one who uses force, obtains a sixth part of the merit or demerit.
The king receives a sixth share of the merit and demerit from his subjects.

The teacher [receives] from the disciple, the husband from the wife, and the father from the son.
A woman also receives half the merit of her husband,

if she constantly conforms to his mind and brings him satisfaction.
When one performs meritorious acts such as giving through the hand of another,

the agent claims a sixth share, except in the case of a servant or son.
A grantor of a livelihood claims an eighth share of the merit of the recipient of the livelihood,
provided he does not require service for himself or for another.

The venerable Kṛṣṇa said:
Thus, even merit and demerit accumulated by others constantly pass [to someone else] without being bestowed.
Listen to this excellent legendary history of old, which brings great merit.

6.113.m:
The venerable Kṛṣṇa said:
Formerly, a brāhmaṇa named Dhaneśvara lived in the city of Avantī,
fallen from sacred duties, intent on sin, and exceedingly evil-minded.

His livelihood was based on false dealing and selling flavored liquids, blankets, skins, and the like;
his mind was attached to theft, courtesans, drinking liquor, and gambling.

Going from country to country for the sake of buying and selling,
that Dhaneśvara once arrived at the city of Māhiṣmatī.

It was built by Mahiṣa formerly; therefore it became Māhiṣmatī,
where the sin-destroying Narmadā shines with its rampart-like banks.

Seeing there the men observing the vows of Kārttika who had come from various villages,
he lived [there] for one month engaged in trade.

Constantly wandering on the banks of the Narmadā for the sake of trade,
he saw the brāhmaṇas bathed and devoted to recitation of prayers and worship of deities.

Some reading the Purāṇa, some devoted to listening to it,
and [others] dedicated to praising Viṣṇu with dance, song, and instruments;

some marked with the seals of Viṣṇu, wearing garlands and tulasī;
filled with curiosity, Dhaneśvara saw [them] here and there.

Wandering there constantly, by seeing, touching, and speaking
with the Vaiṣṇavas, he gained the hearing of the name of Viṣṇu and the like.

Having stayed there thus for a month, he then saw the vigil for Hari
being performed by the devotees during the concluding rite of Kārttika.

Then on the full moon day he saw various kinds of worship and the like,
giving of fees, feeding, and the offering of lamps by those observing the vow.

Then at sunset he saw the festival of lamps
being performed to please the enemy of Tripura.

Because on that [tithi] the burning of the Triple City was done by Śiva,
therefore a great festival is performed by devotees on that lunar day.
Whoever conceives of any distinction between me and Rudra,

All his meritorious deeds would become fruitless, without a doubt. / Looking at the dancing and other performances there, that Dhaneśvara wandered about.

Just then, bitten by a black serpent, he fell down in distress.
Seeing him fallen, the people, filled with compassion, gathered around him.

Then they sprinkled his face with water mixed with tulasī.
Then, when his body was abandoned, Yama's attendants bound him

and, being tormented with whip strikes, angrily led him to Saṃyaminī.
Seeing him, Citragupta rebuked him and then reported

to Yama the evil deed done by him since childhood.
Citragupta said:
Not the least good deed is seen [done by him] anywhere from childhood.

His wickedness cannot be described by the Sun even in a hundred years.
This wicked man is seen to be an embodiment of sin alone, O Lord.

Therefore let him be thoroughly boiled in hell for the duration of a kalpa.
The venerable Kṛṣṇa said:
Hearing such words, Yama spoke out of anger to his servants,

showing a form of his own whose brilliance resembled the fire of cosmic dissolution.
Yama said:
O guardian of ghosts, lead him away, beaten with your own mallets,

and throw him swiftly into Kumbhīpāka, which is noisy with boiling oil.
As soon as he was thrown in there, it became cool,
Just as formerly the fire of the Kumbhīpāka [hell cooled] upon the throwing of Prahlāda, / seeing that great marvel, the ruler of the spirits was filled with astonishment.

Coming with haste, he then recounted all that to Yama.
Hearing the marvel reported by the guardian of ghosts,

Yama said, 'Ah, what is this?' and reflected on it carefully.
Just then, Nārada arrived there, laughing and in haste.

Duly honored by Yama, he looked at him and spoke these words:
Nārada said:
“This man is not fit to experience hells, O son of the Sun-god,

because there arose for him an action that averts hell.
A person who sees, touches, or speaks with those of meritorious deeds

invariably gains a sixth part of that merit.
Because through countless associations he did [this] for Hari,

for a month with those who observe the Kārtika vow, he therefore shares in the portion of merit.
One who performs service for them enjoys the merit of the entire vow.

Therefore, the merit arising from his Ūrja vow is beyond count.
Viṣṇu, who is fond of true devotees,

destroys all the sins—even great ones—of men who observe the Kārtika vow.
Moreover, in the end, by means of His names and with waters mixed with tulasī,

this man received the favor of Vaiṣṇavas, wherefore he will not be cooked in hell at all.
Therefore, with his sins destroyed, he is worthy to attain the good path.

Just as an encounter with suffering in hell is obtained by wet and dry sins,
so an encounter with the enjoyment of heaven is obtained through good deeds.

Therefore, possessing merit free from desire, stationed in the realm of the yakṣas,
he, having seen all the hells, may experience the fruits of his sins.”

Lord Kṛṣṇa said:
Having spoken thus, when Nārada departed, Yama, whose [knowledge of] that virtuous deed was awakened by hearing his speech, / then again sent that brāhmaṇa with his servant, intending to show him all the hosts of hells.

Thus ends the one hundred and thirteenth chapter, in the Tale of Dhaneśvara, in the dialogue between glorious Kṛṣṇa and Satyabhāmā, in the Kārttikamāhātmya of the Uttarakhaṇḍa in the glorious Padma Mahāpurāṇa, in the collection of fifty-five thousand [verses].

6.114.m:
Lord Kṛṣṇa said:
Then, taking Dhaneśvara to the hells, the lord of the ghosts spoke,
intending to show them all, being Yama’s attendant at that time.

The lord of the ghosts said:
“Behold these dreadful, terrifying hells, O Dhaneśvara,
in which evildoers are perpetually cooked by Yama’s servants.

This hell, dreadful to behold, is called Taptavāluka,
in which these sinners, their bodies burned, cry out.

Men who do not honor guests who come hungry and exhausted to their house at the end of the vaiśvadeva,
are indeed cooked by their own deed.

Those who strike teachers, the fire, brāhmaṇas, gods, and consecrated kings with their feet—
these are they, their feet scorched away.

This hell has six divisions and is entered through various sins.
Likewise, the second great hell is Andhatāmisra.

Behold: the body of an evildoer is pierced by needle-faced,
horrible-mouthed worms that come into contact with it, O twice-born!

This one also exists in sixteen forms, with dogs, crows, wild beasts, and birds.
Sinful mortals who pierce the vital spots of others are cooked in them.

This third hell, terrible to behold, is Krakaca,
where these sinful mortals are sawn asunder with saws.

It is arranged in six varieties, beginning with the Sword-leaved Forest.
Men who cause separation [of others] from their wives, sons, and the rest,

and from other dear ones—those men are cooked here.
Being cut by sword-leaves, having fled in fear of being severed,

behold: the sinners are cooked, crying out this way and that.
This fourth hell, known as Argalā, is exceedingly dreadful.

Behold: bound with various snares by Yama’s servants,
beaten with clubs and other weapons, those sinners cry out.

Men who obstruct good people, brāhmaṇas, and others in this world—
those sinners are cooked by Yama’s servants by seizing their necks and other means.

This one too exists in six varieties, through types of execution and other tortures.
Behold the fifth hell, named Kūṭaśālmali,

where these silk-cotton trees and others stand glowing like burning coals, O twice-born,
where these men are cooked in sixteen ways with tortures.

Behold this wonderful sixth hell, of blood and pus,
[for those] who are always devoted to other men's wives, others' wealth, and injury to others,

where sinful men are cooked face downward.
These who ate uneatables, engaged in slander, malicious gossip, and the like,

broken and beaten, utter terrifying cries.
This one also stands in six forms, filled with repulsive odors.

The seventh hell, dreadful to behold, is Kumbhīpāka;
behold it, O Dhaneśvara, in sixteen forms with oil and other substances,

where great sinners are boiled by Yama’s servants
for many thousands of years, with surfacing and submerging.

Behold these Raurava hells, forty-two in number.
A sin committed unintentionally is called dry; that done intentionally is said to be wet.

They are established in two types through wet, dry, and other sins,
and exist in separate divisions numbering eighty-four.

That which is miscellaneous, that causing exclusion from row-sharing, causing defilement,
and causing loss of caste, likewise what is called a secondary sin,

excessive sin, and mortal sin—sin is remembered as sevenfold.
By these [sins] they are cooked in the seven hells in due order.

Because your association was with those observing the Kārtika vow,
these hells have indeed been removed by the accumulation of that merit.”

Lord Kṛṣṇa said:
Having shown the hells thus, the lord of the ghosts then conveyed him,
Dhaneśvara, to the realm of the yakṣas; afterwards he resided there.

He became an attendant of Kubera, remembered as Dhanayakṣa,
in whose name the son of Gādhi made a holy ford in Ayodhyā.

Such indeed is the power of this Kārtika [month], which grants liberation and causes release,
since even one who has accumulated many sins attains liberation merely by seeing one observing the vow.

6.115.m:
Sūta said:
Having spoken thus to his dearly beloved Satyabhāmā, Vāsudeva
went to his mother's house to perform the evening twilight rituals and other rites.

Thus the power of this Kārtika, which destroys sins,
has been declared; it continually pleases Viṣṇu and always grants enjoyment and liberation.

Keeping vigil for Hari, morning ablution, tending the tulasī,
completion rites, and the offering of lamps—these are the vows in Kārtika.

By these five vows the Kārtika vow is made complete.
One attains that declared fruit which yields the fruits of enjoyment and liberation.

The sages said:
“This rite of Kārtika, dear to Viṣṇu and granting great fruit,
purifying and destroying sins, has been duly spoken by you, O Lomaharṣaṇa.

It should certainly be performed by men seeking liberation,
or indeed by those desiring enjoyment, as it averts attained misery.

This being so, if someone engaged in the vow is in distress,
or stranded in a difficult forest, or afflicted by illnesses,
how is that auspicious Kārtika vow to be properly performed by him?”

Sūta said:
“Since it yields exceedingly great fruit, and how it must be performed by men,
all that I will tell. Listen, O best of sages!

One should keep vigil for Hari in a temple of Viṣṇu or Śiva;
in the absence of a shrine to Śiva or Viṣṇu, even in any temple of the gods.”
And whoever is in an impenetrable forest, or wherever one may go, / one should then perform [it] at the root of an aśvattha tree, or even in tulasi groves.
By singing the foremost names of Viṣṇu in the presence of Viṣṇu, / a mortal obtains the fruit of giving a thousand cows.
And a man who plays musical instruments obtains the fruit of a Vājapeya sacrifice; / a dancer obtains the fruit arising from bathing in all sacred waters.
A man who gives material goods to them obtains all this merit; / through praise and beholding, he indeed obtains a sixth part of that.
When one in distress cannot obtain even water for bathing, / or is sick, one should perform purification with the names of Viṣṇu.
One observing a vow who is unable to perform the concluding rite / should feed brāhmaṇas according to one's capacity, for the completion of the vow.
Because it yields the greatest fruit, it should never be abandoned by men; / brāhmaṇas on earth are the very form of Viṣṇu, whose form is unmanifest.
Through their satisfaction I would always be well-pleased, without a doubt. / When unable to give a lamp, one should trim another's lamp.
Or one should diligently protect them from wind and the like. / In the absence of tulasī plants, one should worship a Vaiṣṇava twice-born.
Because Viṣṇu is always present in his own devotees. / In the absence of all [these], one observing a vow should perform [service] to brāhmaṇas, or cows,
or service to an aśvattha and a banyan tree, for the completion of the vow.
The sages said: / How have the aśvattha and the banyan been made equal to cows and brāhmaṇas by you? / Why are they made more worthy of worship than all trees?
Sūta said: / The Blessed Lord Viṣṇu himself has the form of the aśvattha, without a doubt; / likewise the banyan has the form of Rudra, and the palāśa bears the form of Brahmā.
Beholding, worshipping, and serving them is traditionally remembered as removing sin; / it certainly causes the destruction of sorrow, misfortune, disease, and wicked beings.
The sages said: / How did Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśvara come to the state of trees? / Tell this, O omniscient one, for great is our doubt here.
Sūta said: / Formerly, when Pārvatī and Śiva were indeed engaged in sexual union, / Agni was sent by the gods in the form of a brāhmaṇa to cause an obstacle.
Then Pārvatī was angered and cursed the dwellers of heaven, / trembling with rage at that time due to the loss of the pleasure of sexual festival:

Pārvatī said:
Even these worms, insects, and other creatures know the pleasure of sexual union. / Because of creating an obstacle to that, O gods, you shall indeed become plants!

Sūta said:
Thus, with an enraged mind, that Pārvatī cursed the gods; / therefore all the hosts of gods truly became trees.

Therefore these two, Viṣṇu and Maheśvara, both became the bodhi and vaṭa trees, O best of sages! / The bodhi tree, however, obtained touchability on the day of the son of the Sun, but untouchability because of its conjunction with the viṣṭi [period] of the son of the Sun.

6.116.m: And how did it attain touchability on the day of Saturn? / You ought to tell us all this in detail.

Sūta said:
Of the gems that the lords of gods obtained from the churning of the ocean, / the gods gave Śrī and the Kaustubha jewel to Viṣṇu.
As he accepted Lakṣmī as his wife, / Lakṣmī then petitioned that discus-handed Lord:
Lakṣmī said: / Without marrying the elder sister, how can you marry the younger? / Therefore, this elder sister of mine, Alakṣmī, O Madhusūdana—
lead me away afterwards. This is the eternal dharma.
Sūta said: / Having heard those words of hers, that Viṣṇu, the creator of the worlds, / then, to the sage Uddālaka of very long austerities,
according to his own words, gave that Alakṣmī, / who had a stout face, shining white teeth, and bore a body
large, with red eyes and rough reddish-brown hair. / That sage, accepting her according to the word of Viṣṇu, [went] to his own hermitage,
led her to his hermitage, which was filled with the sound of the Vedas, / rich in the fragrant smoke of oblations, and resonant with the recitation of sacred learning.
This dwelling, filled with the sound of the Vedas, is not suitable for me. / I will not enter here, O Brahmin; take me elsewhere without delay!

Uddālaka said:
Why do you not come in? What is pleasing to you here? / And what would be a suitable dwelling for you? Tell that!

Jyeṣṭhā said:
Where there is the sound of the Vedas, and the worship of guests, / or sacrifices, gifts, and the like, I do not dwell there at all.
Where marriage exists through mutual affection, / and where there is worship of ancestors and deities, I do not reside there at all.

Where men are addicted to gambling, steal others' wealth, / and are devoted to others' wives, in that place is my delight.

"Where slaughter of cows and drinking of liquor happen constantly, / and sins such as slaying a brahmin occur—in that place is my delight.
Where there is disrespect toward elders, good people, and Brahmins, / and where harsh speech occurs, there I dwell constantly.

Sūta said:
Having heard her words, Sage Uddālaka became downcast in face; / remembering Viṣṇu's command, he said nothing.
Wherever he went, seeing his worship, she said, / 'I will not come.' Thereupon he too became exceedingly distressed from wandering; / then Uddālaka spoke this word to that Alakṣmī:

Uddālaka said:
O Alakṣmī, stay for a moment at the root of this aśvattha tree, / while I find a dwelling place and come back again.
Sūta said: / Having thus placed her there, Uddālaka then departed; / and when, waiting there for a long time, she did not see him,
then she wept piteously, distressed by her husband's abandonment. / In the world of Vaikuṇṭha, Lakṣmī heard her weeping as she stood there.
Then, with an agitated mind, she petitioned Viṣṇu:

Lakṣmī said:
O Lord, my elder sister is distressed by her husband's abandonment. / Go to comfort her, O compassionate one, if I am dear to you!

Sūta said:
Then Viṣṇu, full of compassion, went there together with Lakṣmī. / He comforted that Alakṣmī and spoke this word:

The venerable Viṣṇu said:
Having resorted to this aśvattha tree, O Alakṣmī, remain here constantly. / For this [tree] is born of a portion of mine; your dwelling has been made [here] by me.
Those householders who worship you, Jyeṣṭhā, every day— / among them this Śrī, your younger sister, shall indeed remain steadfast.

Sūta said:
Those who hear and recite this glorification of the month of Ūrja / shall have their residence in Viṣṇu's city until the dissolution of all beings.

Removing disease, destroying sin, supreme, bestowing good intellect, producing sons, wealth, and the like, / the cause of liberation—indeed there is nothing else on the surface of the earth like Kārttika, which is dear to Viṣṇu.

If a person observes the vow of Ūrja with its regulations, which is dear to Viṣṇu, destroys all defilements, / and brings prosperity of good sons, grandsons, wealth, and grain—what need has he of resorting to and serving sacred waters?

6.117.m:
Sūta said:
Having heard all this, the fortunate Satyabhāmā, the daughter of Satrājit, / then addressed these words to the speech of Hari:

Satyā said:
The glorification of Kārttika has not been heard in detail, O Lord. / How is Kārttika the foremost of all the months?

The venerable Kṛṣṇa said:
Well asked by you with reverence, O Satyā, concerning the Kārttika vow, / which was formerly spoken to Śaunaka by the great-souled Sūta.

Sūta said:
Let it be heard; I shall proclaim that auspicious answer to this question, / which was formerly spoken by the Lord to the inquiring Six-faced One.

Kārttikeya said:
Many secrets of the Lotus-navelled One have been heard / as they were being spoken by you, a devotee of Viṣṇu, O Lord.
For the purpose of rescuing those who have fallen into the ocean of worldly existence, / which is surrounded by the vast waves of sorrow, tell [it] with care.
O best of speakers, [tell] the rule of Kārttika and of the bath, / by which men will cross over the ocean of sorrow, O father!
Explain in full detail the fruit of the Vaiṣṇava dharma, / through the power of which duty one goes to the realm of Viṣṇu.
The glorification of offering lamps, of the muni flower, O you of good vows, / the glorification of gopīcandana, and also of tulasī, O Lord;
the glorification of the mālatī flower, and also speak of lotuses; / the glorification of the fruits of dhātrī, and likewise of damanaka;
the glorification of the ketakī flower, of food offerings, O scorcher of foes, / the glorification of holy waters, and the fruit of bathing in Māgha, O Lord;
tell the fruit, O best of gods, of eating from leaves of the palāśa tree, / the fruit of waving lights, O Sthāṇu, and of kindling another's lamp;
the glorification of the sacred site of Puṣkara, and also of the Boar, O Lord; / the glorification of the śālagrāma stone, and the manner of drawing a svastika;
and tell the fruit of gifts, and of avoiding another's food, / the fruit of fasting for a month, and of renouncing a bed, O Lord!
The glorification of Dīpāvalī and of Prabodhinī, O you of good vows, / and the glorification of Pañcabhīṣma, tell [me] in full detail.
Īśvara said: / Well asked by you, dear one, for the sake of the deliverance of the world; / I shall speak, there is no doubt; there is no Vaiṣṇava equal to you.
By you, a virtuous son, dear one, I have been saved, without a doubt; / unswerving devotion to Keśava always abides in you.
That best of twice-born who gives the Vaiṣṇava duty to men / obtains indeed that merit [equal to] the gift of the earth with its oceans.
It does not equal even a ten-millionth part of the month of Kārttika: / on one side are all the sacred places, and all the gifts are on one side;
on one side are gifts of cows and all sacrifices with their sacrificial fees; / on one side is dwelling in Puṣkara, Kurukṣetra, and the Himālaya;
on one side are the sacred bathing places of Mathurā, Vārāṇasī, and Śūkara; / on one side is Kārttika, dear one, ever dear to Keśava.
Sūta said: / Having spoken thus, O tiger among sages, Hara again uttered words: / I shall narrate in full detail the glorification of bathing in Kārttika.
Īśvara said: / The Kṛta age is declared to be of the brāhmaṇa nature, and the Tretā is itself of the kṣatriya; / the Dvāpara they call of the vaiśya, and the Kali yuga is remembered as the śūdra.
In the Kali age, dear one, there is laxity among human beings in the act of bathing; / nevertheless, I shall describe the bath of Kārttika and Māgha.
A man whose hands and feet, voice, and mind are well-restrained, / who has learning, austerity, and renown—he partakes of the fruit of sacred bathing places.
One lacking faith, a sinful soul, an atheist, one whose mind is divided, / and a rationalistic debater—these five do not partake of the fruit of sacred bathing places.
That twice-born who, having risen in the morning, is always a bather at sacred places, / freed from all sins, attains the supreme Brahman.
Bathing is declared to be fourfold by those who know bathing, O six-faced one: / the wind-related, the water-related, the celestial, and that of Brahmā are thus remembered.
The wind-related bath is [with] cow-dust; the water-related is in the oceans and the like; / that of Brahmā is taught with brāhmaṇa mantras; the celestial is cloud-water with the sun [shining].
And among all baths, the water-related is distinguished there. / A brāhmaṇa, a kṣatriya, and a vaiśya should perform bathing with mantras.
Indeed, silently only for a śūdra and for women, O six-faced one; / a girl, a young woman, an old woman, men, women, and eunuchs—

The blessed lord Mahādeva, whose emblem is the bull, spoke again, / having approached the listener, the six-faced one endowed with devotion:

Īśvara said: / Kārttika is the month of Viṣṇu, and the best among all months; / in this month, the thirty-three gods are present in the Kali age.

In the month of Ūrja, both meals for the twice-born, / an effigy of a cow made of sesame, gold, silver, land, and clothing,

and gifts of cows they will give with wholehearted devotion, O you of good vows; / among all gifts indeed, the gift of a maiden is distinguished.

Men who give a maiden according to rule to a brāhmaṇa / have their dwelling in Vaikuṇṭha as long as there are fourteen Indras.

When the time of pubic hair arrives, Soma enjoys the maiden; / at the time of menstruation, the Gandharvas; and Agni upon the appearance of breasts.

One should marry off a maiden as long as she has not menstruated; / the marriage of an eight-year-old maiden is praised by the wise.

She should be given to a brāhmaṇa who is learned in the Veda, ascetic, / who has directly studied the Vedas, and is a celibate student according to the rule.

This very rule is remembered for a maiden suitable for a groom; / as many hairs as there are on the body of the maiden, O son,

for that many thousands of years he is honored in Rudra’s realm. / A thousand cows are indeed equal to a hundred draft oxen;

a vehicle is equal to ten draft oxen, and a horse is equal to ten vehicles. / The gift of an elephant is superior to thousands of gifts of horses;

the gift of gold is equal to thousands of gifts of elephants; / and the gift of knowledge is equal to thousands of bhāras of gold.

The gift of land is superior, ten million times greater than the gift of knowledge; / and the gift of a cow is superior to thousands of gifts of land.

The gift of food, indeed, is superior to thousands of gifts of cows; / for this entire world, both moving and unmoving, is supported by food.

Therefore, O peacock-mounted one, it should be given with great effort in Kārtika. / Three gifts are equal, and three bear equal fruits.

Kārtikeya said: / You should also tell me of other dharmas, O Mahādeva, / by performing which a man, having washed away all sins, becomes a god.

Sūta said: / Thus questioned, Śambhu then began to speak again. / After praising it in many ways as far [as possible], listen to that, O you whose wealth is asceticism!

6.117.m:
The Lord said: / Whoever avoids food provided by others when the observance is undertaken in Kārtika— / merely by avoiding others' food, he obtains the fruit of a Cāndrāyaṇa vow.

Seeing that Kārtika has arrived, whoever avoids food provided by others, / day by day, that man obtains the fruit of a Kṛcchra penance.

In Kārtika one should avoid oil; in Kārtika one should avoid honey; / in Kārtika one should avoid bell-metal, and especially communal food.

From eating meat just once, he attains a demonic birth; / he is thoroughly cooked in feces for sixty thousand years.

Freed from that, the sinner is born as a village pig eating feces. / But when an observance is undertaken regarding customary foods in Kārtika,

the form of Viṣṇu, the station that grants liberation, is inevitably attained. / There is no month equal to Kārtika; there is no deity higher than Keśava;

there is no scripture like the Veda; there is no sacred bath equal to the Gaṅgā; / there is no conduct equal to truth; there is no age equal to the Kṛta age;

no satisfaction is equal to the tongue; no happiness is like giving; / no friend is equal to dharma; no light is equal to the eye.

Whoever passes the month dear to Dāmodara without vows / should be known as fallen from rituals; he is born in low wombs.

6.117.m: sandals and a parasol should be given in Kārtika, O born of fire. / That man who daily eats on a leaf in Kārtika
does not meet with misfortune as long as the fourteen Indras [endure]; / he obtains the fruit of all desires; he obtains the fruit of all sacred fords.
And he does not see hell, on account of eating from brahma-leaves. / This palāśa [tree] is considered to be Brahmā himself, granting all desires.
One should avoid the middle leaf in Kārtika, O peacock-mounted one. / Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Rudra—these three gods reside in the three leaves:
one should avoid the leaf of Īśvara; Brahmā and Viṣṇu are supreme. / One obtains all merit from eating from the remaining leaves;
from eating from the middle leaf, however, or likewise from drinking the milk of a brown cow, / a man goes to hell, O tiger among sages.
A Śūdra or anyone who consumes the milk of a kapilā cow out of ignorance / becomes purified in [the month of] Kārttika by giving a kapilā cow to a brahmin.
Giving sesame seeds, bathing in a river, always seeing holy persons, / and eating on brahma-leaves in Kārtika grants liberation.
One who observes silence, eats from palāśa leaves, bathes in water, is ever forgiving, / and sleeps on the bare earth in Kārtika destroys sin accumulated over an age.
Whoever keeps vigil at dawn in the month of Kārtika / before Dāmodara, O general, obtains the fruit of a thousand cows.
The fruit [gained] by offering food in the fortnight of the ancestors and water in Jyeṣṭha and Āṣāḍha— / that fruit belongs to men in Kārtika from lighting another's lamp.
From lighting another's lamp and from serving Vaiṣṇavas / in Kārtika, one obtains the fruit of the Rājasūya and Aśvamedha sacrifices.
He who has no river-bathing, no discourse on Viṣṇu, / and no sight of Vaiṣṇavas in Kārtika—it takes away his merit of ten years.
The wise person who remembers Puṣkara with action, mind, and speech / in Kārtika, O tiger among sages, it becomes multiplied a hundred thousand and ten million times.
Prayāga in the month of Māgha, likewise Puṣkara in Kārtika, / and Avantī in the month of Mādhava destroy sin accumulated over an age.
Blessed are those mortals in the world, especially in the Kali age, / who, O Skanda, always perform the worship of Hari in every way.
What is the use of many piṇḍas offered, or śrāddhas at Gayā and the like, O sage? / By that, the ancestors are delivered from hell, there is no doubt.
When bathing Viṣṇu with milk and other substances is performed for the sake of the ancestors, / they attain heaven for ten million kalpas and dwell with the gods.
Those by whom the lotus-eyed Kṛṣṇa is not worshipped in Kārtika— / in ten million births, O chief of brāhmaṇas, Kamalā is not in their home.
They are bitten, robbed, destroyed, and fallen into the abyss of Kali / by whom Hari is not worshipped with devotion using blue and white lotuses.
Whoever worships the lord of gods, the husband of Kamalā, with a single lotus / effects the destruction of sin lasting ten thousand thousands of years.
Thousands of offenses, as well as seven hundred, / the lord of gods forgives when worshipped with a single lotus by one bowed down in reverence.
Whoever worships Hari in Kārtika with a hundred thousand tulasī leaves, / on every leaf, O best of sages, he obtains the fruit of a pearl.
Whatever little is done mixed with the fragrance of tulasī, O son, / Keśava remains pleased for thousands of tens of millions of kalpas.
Whoever bears tulasī taken down from Kṛṣṇa upon his mouth, head, or body / with devotion, O six-faced one, Kali does not touch him.
Whoever wipes his limbs with the sacred remnants taken down from Kṛṣṇa, / he becomes freed from all diseases and likewise from sins, O six-faced one.
Whoever’s body is touched by the remnant ash of Viṣṇu’s [incense], O son, / his sins are destroyed and his ailments come to complete ruin.
Water from the conch, devotion to Hari, the remnants of flowers, water that washed his feet, / sandalwood paste, and the remainder of incense destroy the killing of a brāhmaṇa.

Thus ends the one hundred and eighteenth chapter, entitled "Questions and Answers," in the dialogue between glorious Śiva and Kārttikeya, in the Kārttikamāhātmya of the Uttarakhaṇḍa in the glorious Padma Mahāpurāṇa, in the collection of fifty-five thousand [verses].

6.120.m: The Lord said: / Listen to the glorification of bathing in Māgha, O best of Bhāgavatas! / There is no devotee of Viṣṇu equal to you in this world, O highly wise one.
Whatever fruit a mortal obtains by seeing Hari at Cakra-tīrtha / and Keśava in Mathurā, that fruit is obtained by bathing in Māgha.
With senses conquered, mind pacified, and endowed with righteous conduct, / one who bathes in the month of Māgha does not enter worldly existence again.
The venerable Kṛṣṇa said: / And I shall tell you the glorification of Śūkara, / merely by knowing which my constant presence [is obtained].
Sūta said: / Having spoken thus, the Lord Kṛṣṇa spoke at length to Satyabhāmā. / I shall declare that; hear it, O you whose wealth is asceticism!
The venerable Kṛṣṇa said: / In the temple of Hari known as Śūkara, five yojanas in extent, / any living being residing therein—even a donkey—becomes four-armed.
Three thousand hands, three hundred hands, / and three hands: such is ordained as the measure of Śūkara.
Austerity that one performs elsewhere for sixty thousand years: / one obtains that fruit, O goddess, in half a prahara at Śūkara.
At Sannihatyā in Kurukṣetra, when the sun is seized by Rāhu, / the fruit of giving a tulāpuruṣa is celebrated;
it is declared to be tenfold at Kāśī, a hundredfold at Veṇī, / and a thousandfold at the confluence of the Gaṅgā and the ocean;
and it should be known to be endless at Śūkara, the temple of Hari. / One gives a hundred thousand elsewhere according to rule, O Kārtikeya;
by a single gift given here at Śūkara, it becomes equal to that. / Likewise at Śūkara, at Veṇī, and at the confluence of the Gaṅgā and the ocean,

by bathing just once, a man wipes away the murder of a brāhmaṇa. / In ancient times the seven-islanded earth was obtained by Alarka, / having heard the glorification of the field of Śūkara, O six-faced one.
O Lord, I wish to hear the highest vow among vows: / the rule of the month-long fast and its appropriate fruit;
how the practice of the vow should be performed by men according to rule, / how it is begun originally, and how it is properly concluded;
and for what duration it must be performed: declare that, O Maheśvara. / Explain to me in detail this vow that bestows happiness and prosperity, O sinless one.
The venerable Rudra said: / O son of the fire-god, all that you have asked is excellent; I shall declare it, O sinless one. / Hear from me as I speak with devotion, O best of the wise.
Just as Viṣṇu is among the gods, the sun among luminous bodies, / Meru among mountain peaks, and the son of Vinatā among birds;
just as the Gaṅgā is among holy places, and the merchant among subjects; / even so is the month-long fast the best of all vows.
Whatever merit is found in all vows, in all holy places, / and whatever arises from all gifts, the observer of the month-long fast obtains.
Through various sacrifices such as the Agniṣṭoma with abundant priestly gifts, / one does not attain that merit which comes from fasting for a month.
Chanting, sacrifice, gifts, austerities, and ancestral oblations have been accomplished by him / who observes the month-long fast in accordance with the rule.
Intending a Vaiṣṇava sacrifice and worshipping Janārdana, / one should perform the month-long fast after obtaining the guru’s command.
Having performed all the meritorious Vaiṣṇava vows as prescribed, / such as the twelfth-day observances, one should then fast for a month.
Having performed the Atikṛcchra, the Pārāka, and then the Cāndrāyaṇa penance, / one should observe a month-long fast by the command of the guru and the brahmins.
Having fasted on the eleventh lunar day of the bright half of Āśvina, / one should undertake this vow for thirty days.
A man who, having worshipped Vāsudeva, fasts for the entire / month of Kārttika shall partake of the fruit of liberation.
In the abode of Acyuta, with devotion at the three junctures of the day, with auspicious white water-lilies, / jasmine, blue water-lilies, and fragrant red lotuses;
anointing him with flowers, uśīra, camphor, and excellent sandalwood, / one should worship Janārdana with food offerings, cakes, lamps, and the like.
With mind, action, and speech, one should worship the Garuda-bannered deity; / performing this, a man, a woman, or a widow, with great devotion and senses restrained,
should constantly converse about the names of Viṣṇu day and night; / praise of Viṣṇu should be uttered with devotion, free from false talk.
Endowed with compassion for all beings, of peaceful conduct, non-injurious, / whether sleeping or seated outdoors, he should glorify Vāsudeva.
He should avoid remembering, seeing, smelling, tasting, / or speaking of food, dwelling near it, and receiving morsels.
Anointing the body, anointing the head, betel, and cosmetics— / one observing the vow should abandon all these and whatever else is forbidden.
One observing the vow should touch nothing, should not disturb one who acts improperly, / and remaining in a deity's temple, should certainly not live as a householder.
Having performed the month-long fast according to the prescribed rule, / a man, a woman, a widow, or a virtuous wife should worship Vāsudeva.
Thus, neither less nor more, for thirty days is this vow; / having observed the month-long fast with self-restraint and conquered senses,
he should then worship the holy Garuda-bannered deity on the twelfth lunar day; / he should worship him with flower garlands, perfumes, incense, and ointments.
With garments, ornaments, and musical instruments a man should please Acyuta; / he should bathe Hari with devotion using water from sacred tirthas and sandalwood.
His limbs anointed with sandalwood, adorned with incense and flowers; / and having fed the best of brāhmaṇas with gifts of garments and the like,
he should give them priestly gifts and, prostrating himself, ask for forgiveness. / Thus having observed the month-long fast and worshipped Janārdana,
and having fed brāhmaṇas, he is glorified in the world of Viṣṇu. / Thus, at the end of the month-long fast, having gathered thirteen brāhmaṇas,
he should then dismiss them; hear by what rule: / Having fasted on the eleventh lunar day, he should cause a Vaiṣṇava sacrifice to be performed.
Having worshipped the Lord of gods, Hari, with the permission of the preceptor, / and having honoured Him according to one's ability, and likewise having saluted the guru,
he should then feed brāhmaṇas after prostrating before them— / those of pure family and conduct, intent on the worship of Viṣṇu.
Having worshipped all thirteen and having fed them, / [giving] betel, pairs of garments, food, and clothing,
ascetic meditation bands, cords, and sacred threads / he should give to the eminent brāhmaṇas, having worshipped and bowed to them.
Then, according to his capacity, he should venerate a bed furnished with mattresses, / covered, auspicious, excellent, adorned and provided with a pillow.
Having had an image of himself fashioned of gold according to his means, / he should place it upon that bed after worshipping it with garlands and the like.
A seat, wooden sandals, an umbrella, a pair of garments, shoes, / and sacred flowers he should arrange upon the bed.

'Lacking mantra, lacking rite, lacking everything, O best of brāhmaṇas— / may everything attain completeness by the grace of your words.' / The rule of the month-long fast has been fully declared.

Having heard this speech, the son of Pavāka (Kārtikeya) asked again / about the worship of the Śālagrāma stone. Listen to that, O ascetics rich in penance!

Kārtikeya said: / O Lord, best among yogins, all dharmas have been heard by me. / Speak to me in detail, O Master, about the worship of the Śālagrāma stone.

The Lord (Śiva) said: / Well done, well done, O highly wise one, in asking me this! / I shall explain that; let it be heard, O dear one!

In the Śālagrāma stone indeed, the three worlds with all that moves and does not move, / O great-minded one, O Mahāsena, constantly reside united.

By him by whom it is seen, bowed down to, bathed, and worshipped, / merit multiplied ten-millionfold of a sacrifice, and the fruit of ten million cows, is attained.

By him, O child, the extremely terrifying dwelling in the womb is severed, / by whom the water of Viṣṇu's Śālagrāma stone is constantly drunk.

Even one who is attached to desire and constantly devoid of devotional disposition, / having worshipped the Śālagrāma stone, O son, becomes imperishable.

6.120.m:
The image that is the Śālagrāma stone destroys tens of millions of sins / when remembered, praised aloud, meditated upon, worshipped, and bowed down to.

Seeing the Śālagrāma stone, sins depart in manifold ways, / just as herds of deer in the forest flee out of fear upon seeing a lion.

A human being, making a reverent bow during the worship of the Śālagrāma stone / either with devotion or without devotion, attains liberation.

There is no fear of Yama, nor of death and birth, / for a man who constantly performs the worship of the Śālagrāma stone.

With scents, water for washing feet, offerings of guest-water, oblations of food, with lamps, incenses, unguents, / with songs, musical instruments, and praises, the worship of the Śālagrāma stone

which a person performs, devoted to devotion in the Kali age, / he rejoices in the abode of Viṣṇu for ten million thousands of kalpas.

When even a single bow to the Śālagrāma stone is made by men with true feeling, / how could they remain ordinary mortals—those men on earth who are devoted to me?

Those who, claiming to be my devotees, are severe sinners and do not bow down to my Lord, / Vāsudeva—they are not to be known as my devotees, but as deluded by sin.

And he who, even having become my devotee, eats on the eleventh day (Ekādaśī), / that murderer of mine goes indeed to the hell of blinding darkness.

The touching of my liṅga is to be performed; no other purification is prescribed. / That lunar day which is dear to Viṣṇu is also beloved of me.

A mortal who does not fast on it is a sinner worse than an outcaste. / In the Śālagrāma stone, however, I always reside, O son.

His own place was given to me by the pleased God (Viṣṇu) out of devotion. / Whatever fruit there is when I am worshipped with thousands of tens of millions of lotuses,

that fruit is multiplied ten-millionfold by the worship of the Śālagrāma stone. / I have not been worshipped by those mortals, I have not been bowed down to by those men,

by whom worship of the Śālagrāma stone has not been performed in the world of mortals. / But he who performs worship of me before the Śālagrāma stone,

by him I, the general of the gods, have been worshipped for twenty-one cosmic ages. / What is the use of hundreds of liṅgas worshipped if they are devoid of devotion to Viṣṇu?

If the Śālagrāma stone image is not worshipped, O my child, / my food offering, leaf, flower, fruit, and water are unworthy.

Before the Śālagrāma stone, however, everything attains purity. / Having consumed food offered to other gods, a twice-born should perform the Cāndrāyaṇa penance;

having eaten Keśava's food offering, he obtains the fruit of ten million sacrifices. / With the water from the feet of the God, those possessed of ten million murders

6.120.m:
the worship of the Śālagrāma stone should be performed out of that devotion to me. / Where Keśava resides in the form of a Śālagrāma stone,

there are the gods, demons, and yakṣas, and the fourteen worlds.

Whatever fruit one might obtain through tens of millions of all praises of the gods, / that good deed is obtained in the Kali age just by praising Keśava.

Once satisfied with a funeral rice-ball before the Śālagrāma stone, / his ancestors reside [in bliss]—there is no counting [the years] there.

What need is there of consuming thousands of the five products of the cow / for those men who drink with devotion the water of the Śālagrāma stone?

When an expiation arises, what use are gifts, what use are fasts / and well-performed Cāndrāyaṇa penances, once the foot-water of Hari has been drunk?

He who sets up in a pond an image reclining on the water— / what need is there for him to worship tens of millions of other gods?

The gods headed by Viṣṇu indeed converse there together. / There is a measure for all good deeds, O child,

but there is no measure of the fruit of worshipping the Śālagrāma stone. / He who gives to a brāhmaṇa devotee of Viṣṇu a stone originating from Śālagrāma,

by him sacrifice has been performed with hundreds of sacrificial rites. / Even while residing in his own home, day after day he has bathed in the Ganges;
